content:
I'm trying to formalize the proof of the fact that the operator norm of a positive linear functional between C*-algebras is equal to the limit of that functional evaluated at the approximate identity. The traditional statement of this theorem uses nets and relies on the argument that for an increasing net that is bounded above, the limit (and consequently liminf) must both be equal to the limsup.

Is there an equivalent of this principle in Mathlib that is appropriate for use with filters? Is the concept of an increasing filter even meaningful, and is there an idiomatic way to state that?

I'm especially confused because the theorem docs#Filter.IsIncreasingApproximateUnit, doesn't actually seem to make any mention of the approximate identity being increasing. Instead, it just states that it is eventually non-negative and bounded within the unit ball. I think the theorem docs#CStarAlgebra.directedOn_nonneg_ball perhaps combined with docs#CStarAlgebra.hasBasis_approximateUnit is giving some kind of hint about how this might be done, but I have been unable to piece it together so far.

Gregory Wickham said:

Is there an equivalent of this principle in Mathlib that is appropriate for use with filters?

I wouldn't be able to find a theorem unless I know what "increasing filter" means. But certainly we have that a bounded monotone sequence of reals has a limit (see docs#tendsto_atTop_ciSup).

Gregory Wickham said:

Is the concept of an increasing filter even meaningful, and is there an idiomatic way to state that?

I like to think of filters as generalized sets. Is the concept of an increasing set meaningful? It doesn't seem so to me. Perhaps you can provide more details of the argument, so we can see how "increasing net" comes into the picture.
@Monica Omar already has a proof of this result. I think it doesn't have any dependencies. Monica, do you want to PR that?
It currently depends on PositiveContinuousLinearMap, so Jireh maybe you want to PR that first? :)

@Gregory Wickham, I also have the iff version: given an docs#Filter.IsIncreasingApproximateUnit l and a bounded linear functional f, we get that f is positive (i.e., docs#Monotone) iff l.Tendsto (f ·) (𝓝 ‖f‖).
Ah, I forgot about that. Okay yes, I'll do that Monday.

It's great that you already have those ready! Is there anything else beyond that that you'll also be finished with soon? I'm just trying to finish the cyclic vector bit of the gns construction, but if you're already almost there, I can leave it to you.

Once you PR those theorems, can you comment the PR numbers here, just so I can refer to them?
